w: Offered in threads on building communities and movements; one commenter calls it worth reading and points to Godin's interviews as a shorter route.
ab: For anyone starting a community or movement
Short and easy to read
Marketing-flavored and light on evidence

q.t: Seth Godin talks about tribes in his book, called, well...Tribes[0]. Worth reading.

s: A comprehensive one-volume biography of Napoleon Bonaparte drawing on his recently published letters.
w: HN readers call it a highly informative and enjoyable history that is also gigantic. One reader gave up because of its sheer size.
ab: For readers who want a deep, readable Napoleon biography
Huge book, about 800 pages
Some find the size daunting

q.t: It's one of those rare works of history that is both highly informative and a real pleasure to read.

t: Snakes in Suits: When Psychopaths Go to Work
s: A look at how manipulative, psychopathic individuals operate and advance inside companies.
w: Frequently suggested in threads about toxic executives and workplace manipulation. Commenters call it enlightening on non-violent psychopaths who chase money and power.
ab: For people dealing with manipulative coworkers or bosses
By a leading psychopathy researcher and a business psychologist
Some recommenders had not read it themselves

q.t: It turns out many people like that just aren't violent. Instead, they like money and power.

s: Apple's compact desktop workstation with Apple silicon Max and Ultra chips and large unified memory.
w: Recommended lately as a quiet, power-efficient machine with lots of unified memory for running local LLMs and as a home server. One commenter had a grounding annoyance with the plug.
ab: For developers running big models or heavy workloads locally
Up to very large unified memory configurations
Has a fan, unlike the Mac mini; one plug/GFCI complaint

q.t: for a silent, relatively power-efficient yet powerful

s: A wireless ergonomic mouse with programmable buttons, a thumb wheel, app-specific profiles and multi-device switching.
w: HN developers like its programmable back/forward buttons for code navigation, large hand-friendly shape and multi-computer flow. It was also recommended for reducing wrist and hand strain.
ab: For heavy desk users and developers
Many programmable buttons and per-app layouts
Big shape; some prefer the Lift or Vertical for ergonomics

q.t: the forward/backward button on mx master 3s is extremely helpful navigating code

s: Apple's compact, lower-priced iPhone line with a small screen and the internals of a recent flagship.
w: Recommended by HN readers who want a small phone with good battery life, or a more minimal phone. The small screen is the trade-off.
ab: For people who want a pocketable phone
Good battery life for its size, per commenters
Small screen is poor for video

q.t: Got one from work and it's perfect for me -- small, battery lasts more than a day.

s: A novel about a Russian aristocrat sentenced to house arrest in Moscow's Hotel Metropol, living through decades of Soviet history.
w: HN readers across several years' reading threads rank it among their best: well-written, charming, with endearing characters, and enough to start a Russia reading kick.
ab: For readers who like charming, character-driven historical fiction
Gentle pace, rich writing
Author has other novels in similar spirit

q.t: blew me away by the quality of the writing, the endearing characters and the charming setting

s: A near-future science fiction thriller about a man whose genome is altered, giving him enhanced abilities with dangerous consequences.
w: Fans of Project Hail Mary and Blake Crouch's other books call it a fun, fast, easy read, and several put it alongside Dark Matter and Recursion.
ab: For readers who like page-turning hard-ish sci-fi
Fast pace, accessible prose
Plot leans thriller over deep science

q.t: they were all really fun easy reads. Highly recommended.

s: A concise introduction to quantum mechanics with the real math, based on Susskind's Stanford continuing-studies lectures.
w: HN commenters recommend it as the shortest route to actually understanding quantum mechanics with real math. It is accessible but grounded in the true principles used in physics.
ab: For adults with calculus and linear algebra who want real physics
Part of the Theoretical Minimum series
You have to do the math; not light reading

q.t: written to be relatively accessible, but is actually grounded in the real principles and math used in physics

t: UFOs: Generals, Pilots, and Government Officials Go on the Record
s: A journalist's compilation of official UFO reports and testimony from military and government figures.
w: Recommended to skeptics as a sober take on documented reports of unidentified aerial phenomena, avoiding both believers and debunkers.
ab: For skeptical readers curious about official UFO records
Focuses on testimony from pilots and officials
Written before recent disclosure reports

q.t: In a field where many of the books are written by either true believers or debunkers

s: Shows how a small group of scientists used the same tactics of manufactured doubt to delay action on tobacco, acid rain, ozone and climate change.
w: HN commenters recommend it to explain how industry-funded doubt works on health and climate, and describe it as an almost legal or academic account.
ab: For readers who want the history of manufactured doubt
Heavily sourced and academic in tone
Focused on the US

q.t: Merchants of Doubt [1] goes into the pattern in an almost legal/academic way

s: A narrative of the Microsoft team that created DirectX and fought inside the company.
w: Recommended as a fascinating look at Microsoft internals and DirectX history.
ab: Inside story of DirectX
Narrative nonfiction
1999 view of events

q.t: I thought Renegades of the Empire was a fascinating look into the internal machinations at Redmond and a bit of DirectX history too

by: W. J. King, James G. Skakoon
s: A short guide to the unspoken professional rules of working as an engineer, covering teamwork, bosses, communication and judgment.
w: HN commenters recommend it as a quick soft-skills primer they wish they had read at the start of their career, with a note that parts are dated.
ab: For new engineers learning workplace norms
Very short, under 70 pages in the updated edition
Some advice is dated

q.t: It's a bit dated but has a lot of helpful advice - I wish I had read it when I started my career.

s: A hands-on book that walks through building a C compiler step by step, with test suites, in the implementation language of your choice.
w: HN compiler fans list it among recent practical compiler books; one notes it spends time on types and pointers, which other compiler books often skip.
ab: For programmers wanting to build a real compiler
Implementation language of your choice
Focuses on a practical C subset

q.t: Writing a C Compiler by Nora Sandler, language agnostic for the implementation.

t: Compact Data Structures: A Practical Approach
s: A textbook survey of succinct and compact data structures that store data in near-minimal space while still supporting fast queries.
w: HN commenters in compression and data structure threads point to it as an excellent survey of the field, the book for anyone into succinct structures.
ab: For readers into algorithms, compression and indexing
Survey of succinct data structures by a leading researcher
Technical, academic textbook

q.t: Navarro's book Compact Data Structures is an excellent survey of this literature!

t: Expert Political Judgment: How Good Is It? How Can We Know?
s: Tetlock's two-decade study of expert forecasters, finding that most pundits perform barely better than chance, with the hedging fox beating the confident hedgehog.
w: HN cites it whenever punditry, certainty, and prediction come up, as the evidence that confident experts are often the worst forecasters.
ab: For readers interested in forecasting, expertise, and judgment
Academic study with long-term data from experts
Dense academic style; the Superforecasting book is easier

q.t: The basic conclusion is nobody is really that good, but some people are objectively better than others.

s: A guide to designing and running large-scale web infrastructure, covering load balancing, caching, databases and operations.
w: Recommended in threads about learning to scale a service, as a practical introduction with general advice on approaching scaling problems rather than tool-specific recipes.
ab: For web developers whose service is outgrowing one server
Practical advice on approaching scaling problems
Written in 2007; specific tools are dated

q.t: It contains general advice on how to approach problem solving when it comes to building uh, scalable architectures.

s: The story of the Iridium satellite network and how it nearly de-orbited.
w: Recommended as a great history of Iridium.
ab: For space and telecom fans
Business history
Detailed

q.t: Eccentric Orbits is a really great book about their history, especially the near de-orbit with lots of fun tidbits

by: Bryan O'Sullivan, John Goerzen et al.
s: An O'Reilly book teaching Haskell through practical programs: parsing, databases, concurrency and web work.
w: People credit it with changing how they view programming and like its concrete examples. A later commenter warns it's somewhat out of date but still better for practical how-tos than LYAH.
ab: For programmers who want Haskell applied to real tasks
Many concrete code examples
Written in 2008; some libraries and tooling are outdated

q.t: This book has completely changed my view on programming.

t: iOS Programming: The Big Nerd Ranch Guide
s: A hands-on tutorial book for building iOS apps in Objective-C, teaching Cocoa Touch through step-by-step projects.
w: In 2012 and 2013 HN threads on learning iOS, commenters named it as the best book for beginners. One says they were confident enough to build their own things by the second chapter.
ab: For programmers new to iOS who like tutorial-style learning
Hands-on projects with code
Written for Objective-C and iOS 6, so it is badly out of date now

q.t: By the second chapter I felt confident enough to start trying things out on my own and tutorials made a lot more sense.

s: A pair of magnetic tips that turns any USB-C cable into a breakaway connector supporting charging, data and video.
w: Mentioned as a cheap MagSafe-style fix for USB-C laptops. One user confirms all 24 pins work, though another says coworkers found such adapters poor.
ab: For USB-C laptop users wanting a magnetic breakaway
All 24 pins reportedly connected for video, data and power
Quality of these adapters reported as hit or miss

q.t: All 24 pins are connected, so video, data, and power all work as expected.

t: Eats, Shoots & Leaves: The Zero Tolerance Approach to Punctuation
s: A humorous British guide to punctuation, from commas to apostrophes, arguing for care with the rules.
w: Recommended as a fun way to learn punctuation, and the title is the go-to reference when someone misplaces a comma in a thread.
ab: For writers and grammar fans who like a funny tone
British conventions in places
Some find it pedantic; others find it charming

q.t: It too gets berated by some but I enjoyed it and learned a thing or two.

s: A graduate textbook on convex optimization theory, applications and algorithms.
w: Appears on HN reading lists for machine learning and math self-study.
ab: For ML and math students
Rigorous graduate text
Free PDF available from the authors

t: Being Geek: The Software Developer's Career Handbook
s: A career guide for software developers on interviewing, managing up, handling managers and teams, and moving toward management, by the author behind Rands in Repose.
w: HN recommends it as the other Rands book, top notch for devs and for anyone between experienced developer and manager, often listed under non-programming reads.
ab: For developers thinking about career moves and management
Humorous, personal essays
Pairs with Lopp's Managing Humans

q.t: is top notch as well for devs and those living somewhere in-between experienced dev and team manager.

s: A short philosophical essay arguing that modern achievement culture and positivity cause exhaustion and burnout.
w: HN readers recommend it as the best place to start with Han, a quick read that takes aim at the culture of positivity.
ab: For readers curious about contemporary philosophy and work culture
Very short essay, quick to read
Dense academic-leaning ideas

q.t: Takes dead-aim at the culture of positivity and

t: Open Circuits: The Inner Beauty of Electronic Components
s: A photo book of cross-sections and X-rays of electronic components with explanations of how each works.
w: HN readers call it a beautiful, brilliant book that pairs well with teardown posts and component curiosity. One electronics hobbyist worried it was too light but changed his mind after a review.
ab: For electronics fans who love component teardowns and photos
Large-format photography with short explanations
Light on hands-on learning for hobbyists

q.t: It's an absolutely brilliant book

s: A dark, modern fantasy novel about a college student discovering a hidden magic school, first of a trilogy.
w: HN readers who like it say it moved them and made them think, and it gets re-read or gifted. One reader abandoned the first two books out of boredom.
ab: For adult fantasy readers who like a darker, ironic take
First of a trilogy, with a TV series
Slow and bleak; polarizing among HN readers

q.t: they both moved me and made me think

s: A saddle-style active-sitting office chair from HÅG with a high, open seat that supports many sitting positions.
w: HN owners say it encourages movement, fixed their back and leg pain, and holds up for years. It looks odd and costs a lot.
ab: For people who fidget or sit in many positions
Long-lasting build; owners report like-new after years
Pricey and unusual look

q.t: Its design somehow encourages you to change positions regularly, which is important to avoid getting sore.

s: Google's line of Android smartphones known for their camera and clean Android software.
w: HN commenters view the Pixel as hardware roughly on par with the iPhone, with good photos and useful features like Hold For Me. Fit and finish is a notch below Apple for some.
ab: Android phone with strong camera and software features.
Hardware close to iPhone, per commenters.
Limited availability in some countries and assistant quirks.

q.t: The Pixel or any top-end Samsung is equivalent or better than the iPhone in hardware.

t: 7 Powers: The Foundations of Business Strategy
s: A business strategy book that identifies seven sources of durable competitive advantage, like scale economies, network effects and switching costs.
w: HN founders cite it as an authoritative framework for business moats. Several read it in a sitting. One reader was not blown away.
ab: For founders and strategists thinking about moats
Framework with company case studies
Dense; not blow-away for every reader

q.t: I devoured Hamilton Helmer's 7 Powers this year.

s: A fully split membrane keyboard joined by a cable, so each half can be spread to shoulder width and optionally tented.

Halves can be placed shoulder-width apart
Membrane keys feel mushy; tenting needs an extra kit

q.t: Your wrist will thank you for it.

s: Apple's 2022 thin, fanless laptop with an M2 chip, available in 13-inch and later 15-inch sizes.
w: HN users call it the best laptop they have used: light, silent, long battery. Several chose it for travel or to replace older Intel Macs.
ab: For people wanting a light, quiet, long-lasting laptop
Fanless M2 chip with all-day battery
Base RAM and storage are small; upgrades cost extra

q.t: My Macbook Air M2 is the exact opposite of that. Best purchase of the past few years, without a doubt.

s: A compact keyboard with a straight-grid (non-staggered) layout, switchable Dvorak and Colemak modes in hardware, and handy cut-copy-paste keys.

ab: For Dvorak or Colemak typists who want a grid layout
Layout switch happens in the keyboard
Control key placement and double-height shift keys are criticized

q.t: I will join philh and sepeth in saying I really like the TypeMatrix 2030.

t: The Outsiders: Eight Unconventional CEOs and Their Radically Rational Blueprint for Success
s: Profiles of eight CEOs who beat the market by focusing on capital allocation, free cash flow and decentralized management rather than conventional playbooks.

Case studies of Buffett, Malone, Singleton and others
Focus is on mature companies, not startups

t: Common LISP: A Gentle Introduction to Symbolic Computation
s: A beginner-friendly introduction to Common Lisp and symbolic computation, available freely online.
w: HN commenters point to it as the gentle starting book for Common Lisp, noting it is freely available.

Gentle pace with plenty of exercises
Free online version exists

q.t: How about this? It's even freely available nowadays

t: A First Course in Abstract Algebra

Gentle, well-motivated exposition
Not CS-oriented; Kindle edition reviews are poor

Accessible, with arithmetic included
US-focused and written in 2021

s: A full-cast audio dramatization of Neil Gaiman's Sandman comic series, produced by Audible.

ab: For fans of the comic or anyone wanting a dark fantasy audio drama
Full-cast production, released in parts
Needs an Audible account

q.t: Neil Gaiman's Sandman dramatic audiobook (part I) is so good.

s: A short solarpunk novella about a tea monk and a robot who meet in a world where robots left human society generations ago.

Short novella, first of the Monk and Robot books
Quiet, slow, conversation-driven plot

s: A leadership book arguing that great leaders look after their people, drawing on biology, military examples and company culture.

Anecdote-heavy rather than research-based
Sinek's other titles include Start With Why

q.t: Everything by Simon Sinek, but most important for me is

Fast-paced classic travel story
19th-century attitudes toward other cultures

Graphic battle scenes

Two interlocking storylines
Dreamlike and ambiguous ending

Short, introspective German classic
Heavy on symbolism and early 20th-century psychology

s: A short introduction to the science of intelligence research, covering IQ testing, heritability and what intelligence predicts.

Part of a short book series, easy to finish quickly
Brief overview; not a deep technical treatment

s: A journalist's investigation into the rise in teenage girls identifying as transgender, arguing that social influences play a role.

ab: For readers wanting to understand one side of a polarized debate
Journalistic, interview-based approach
Widely criticized by medical and LGBT advocacy groups

q.t: was called one of the best books of the year by the Economist and the London Times

t: Carrying the Fire: An Astronaut's Journeys
s: Michael Collins's memoir of his Gemini and Apollo 11 missions.
w: Described as a deeply influential book, inspiring one commenter to go into aerospace, and cited for what Collins said about single points of failure on Apollo.
ab: For space history and astronaut memoir readers
Firsthand account of Apollo 11 from the command module
Personal and literary tone

q.t: I want to take a moment to write about how much Michael Collins has meant to me.

s: A collection of essays on race, culture and history in America, including a chapter on slavery and the culture of the South.
w: Frequently suggested by commenters in political threads as a core Sowell text, usually next to his other books on economics and discrimination.
ab: For readers interested in race and culture debates from a conservative economist
Essay collection with a strong thesis
Controversial; commenters recommend it mostly within one political camp

q.t: chapter three of Thomas Sowell's Black Rednecks & White Liberals, about the history of slavery.

t: Democracy for Realists: Why Elections Do Not Produce Responsive Government
by: Christopher H. Achen, Larry M. Bartels
s: A political science book arguing that voters choose by group identity and loyalty, not policy, and that the folk theory of democracy is wrong.
w: The HN reference for the argument that most people don't vote on issues. Commenters cite it in threads on demagoguery, misinformation and why elections fail to produce responsive government.
ab: For readers interested in political behavior and voting research
Evidence-heavy academic book
Its conclusions are bleak and contested

q.t: Almost no one votes on the issues.

s: Maister's classic on running consultancies and other professional firms: pricing, leverage, partner management and client work.
w: Software firm owners call it the most accurate and instructive book on running a services business. It appears on lists of books with high signal-to-noise.
ab: For consultants and agency founders
Covers firm economics, leverage and partnership
Aimed at firms, not individual freelancers

q.t: Managing the Professional Service Firm by David Maister is the most accurate and instructive book I've read on the topic

t: Solitude: A Return to the Self
s: A psychiatrist's examination of why solitude matters for creativity, mental health and personal development.
w: Recommended in loneliness and isolation threads as a counter-argument that time alone is valuable and necessary. One user found its treatment of depression and creativity interesting.
ab: For readers curious about the value of being alone
Draws on psychology and the lives of creative people
Originally published in the late 1980s

q.t: It discusses about solitude, its necessity and other related issues like depression in detail.

s: The story of the first transatlantic telegraph cable, from repeated failures to its completion in 1866.
w: HN readers like it as the origin story of the global network their tech sits on: a decade of failures, huge risk and engineering stubbornness.
ab: For people who like engineering history and big infrastructure projects.
Follows Cyrus Field's decade-long push to lay the first cable.
Narrative history rather than a technical text.

q.t: One of the most interesting books I read was mentioned here on HN early this year: A Thread Across the Ocean

t: Programming Rust: Fast, Safe Systems Development
s: An O'Reilly book on Rust covering ownership, traits, concurrency, and unsafe code for systems programmers.
w: Named as an external Rust book alongside The Rust Programming Language. One commenter started with it, while another asks whether the first edition is still relevant.
ab: For programmers learning Rust beyond the official book
Systems-oriented examples
First edition is dated; Rust has changed

q.t: There's several external books. I started from this one (via Safari)

t: Careless People: A Cautionary Tale of Power, Greed, and Lost Idealism
s: A former Facebook policy executive's memoir about her years at the company and the behavior of its leadership.
w: HN commenters recommend it for details on Meta's conduct, including its China ambitions. Interest surged after Meta tried to block the author from promoting it.
ab: For readers interested in Big Tech and Facebook's inner workings
First-person insider memoir
Author's account; Meta disputes it

q.t: Read her book Careless People [1] where she shared many details.

t: The Body: A Guide for Occupants
s: A tour of the human body, its organs and systems, written for general readers with plenty of surprising trivia.
w: Appears on many HN yearly reading lists. Commenters like Bryson's geeky enthusiasm and how hard it is to put down.
ab: For curious general readers wanting a readable biology tour
Packed with trivia and anecdotes, not a medical text
Some commenters mention it only as a to-read

q.t: He geeks out about stuff and showers is with fascinating trivia

s: A post-pandemic novel following a traveling Shakespeare troupe and interlinked lives before and after civilization collapses.
w: A fixture on HN yearly reading lists. Fans find it fabulous, and its distinct, transporting writing keeps drawing readers to other books by the author.
ab: For readers who like literary post-apocalyptic fiction
Reflective and character-driven, not action
Pandemic setting may feel close to home

q.t: the latest, which I thought was fabulous: Station Eleven by Emily St. John Mandel

t: Bowling Alone: The Collapse and Revival of American Community
s: Robert Putnam's study of the decline of social capital and civic engagement in the United States.
w: Cited as a classic on loneliness and declining community, and recommended whenever threads discuss social isolation. Commenters quote its findings on how community ties affect health.
ab: For readers curious about social capital and civic decline
Data-heavy argument about American community
Written in 2000; some of its conclusions are debated

q.t: almost exactly the same conclusions were stated by Putnam in the classic _Bowling Alone_

t: Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products
s: A guide to the Hook Model for designing products people return to habitually.
w: Cited when apps and engagement come up; readers found it eye-opening about behavioral psychology in product design, though some call it manipulative.
ab: For product designers and founders
Short, framework-driven
Ethics of manipulation is a recurring complaint

q.t: is a really interesting read on this subject. For me it was eye-opening to think about app development from a behavioral and psychological perspective

t: The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Complete Guide to Dimensional Modeling
s: The standard reference on dimensional modeling, star schemas and building data warehouses for business intelligence and reporting.
w: HN data and BI folks keep pointing newcomers here as the foundational text on warehouse design, written by one of the field's founders.
ab: For analysts and engineers building reporting databases or BI systems
Covers star schemas, fact and dimension tables, and surrogate keys
Enterprise-flavored and long; read selectively

q.t: Here is an excellent resource if you're interested in this sort of thing

t: Cyberpunk: Outlaws and Hackers on the Computer Frontier
s: Three narratives about early hackers: Kevin Mitnick, Pengo and the Chaos Computer Club, and Robert Tappan Morris, author of the Morris worm.
w: HN commenters recommend it as a companion to The Cuckoo's Egg, telling hacking stories from the hackers' side. It also comes up for its section on the Morris worm.
ab: For readers interested in hacker history and computer security
Covers Mitnick, Pengo and the Morris worm
Written in 1991; narrative is journalistic

q.t: was pretty interesting related reading, as it covers the same story from from the other side

s: A desk controller with customizable LCD keys that trigger shortcuts, macros, app switching and smart-home actions.
w: HN users say it replaced dead macro keyboards and Touch Bars, and use it for audio, lights and app control. People also enjoy writing their own plugins, and there is a Linux open-source driver.
ab: For people who want programmable shortcut buttons
Customizable keys, plugin support, unofficial Linux tools
One commenter found the product pitch confusing

q.t: Stream deck was a surprisingly good buy for me as well

s: App-controlled smart LED bulbs with adjustable color and brightness that work with a hub, voice assistants and automation systems.
w: HN buyers love them for tunable warm light that replaces incandescents and for sunrise alarms that help sleep, even if they cost more.
ab: For people who want tunable, automatable lighting
Warm tones and sunrise alarms are the draw
Pricier than ordinary bulbs

q.t: We use Hue bulbs. They're much more expensive, but we can tune their colours to pretty much exactly what we want.

t: The Facebook Effect: The Inside Story of the Company That Is Connecting the World
s: An authorized, reported history of Facebook's growth from a Harvard dorm project into a global company.
w: HN commenters call it a well-written insider's account and a more accurate telling of Facebook and Zuckerberg than the movie.
ab: For readers interested in Facebook's early history
Written with company cooperation, so sympathetic
Published in 2010; leaves out later years

q.t: It's a great read and a far more accurate book on the history of Facebook

t: Why Buddhism Is True: The Science and Philosophy of Meditation and Enlightenment
s: A journalist argues that core Buddhist ideas about suffering and the self are supported by evolutionary psychology and neuroscience, and makes a secular case for meditation.
w: Science-minded HN readers recommend it as a way into meditation and spirituality without the mysticism. It frames Buddhist insight through evolution and cognitive science.
ab: For skeptical, science-oriented readers curious about meditation
Mixes evolutionary psychology, neuroscience and Buddhist philosophy
Secular take; some readers want more practice instruction

q.t: In essence this book tells why secular Buddhism (secular, western meditation) is actually a very reasonable way of spirituality.

s: A factory-building and automation game where you gather resources, design production lines and defend against alien attacks.
w: HN engineers recommend it for engineering and systems thinking, a great tutorial and runs natively on Linux; several warn it will consume your free time.
ab: For people who like planning, automation and optimization
Native Linux support; buy direct from the developer
Highly time-consuming

q.t: Factorio is great. Too great, I can't play it any more because it sucked up all my free time.

s: A reference on Windows architecture covering processes, threads, memory management, the kernel and security.
w: Named as the book to start with for understanding Windows internals and systems programming.
ab: For systems programmers on Windows
Deep and detailed
Pair with Part 2

q.t: The best start would probably be both parts of Windows Internals:

t: Talent Is Overrated: What Really Separates World-Class Performers from Everybody Else
s: A book arguing that deliberate practice, not innate talent, explains most world-class performance.
w: Recommended in threads about the 10,000-hour idea as a book on how to practice, going a step beyond the rule. Commenters suggest it against the belief that talent cannot be made up for.
ab: For readers interested in deliberate practice and skill-building
Draws on Anders Ericsson's research
Popular-business style rather than a research text

q.t: It explores HOW you practice, a step beyond the 10,000 hour rule.

t: American Nations: A History of the Eleven Rival Regional Cultures of North America
s: A history arguing North America divides into eleven regional cultures with distinct origins, values and politics that shape the country today.
w: Pointed to when people ask why US regions differ so much. One fan called it the best book they read that year, though one reader found it simplistic.
ab: For readers curious about US regional and political divides
Sweeping thesis; critics say it is overly deterministic
Narrative history, easy to read

q.t: It connects a lot of dots. Probably the best book I read/listened to last year.

t: How to Win Friends & Influence People
s: Dale Carnegie's classic 1936 guide to getting along with people, building rapport and persuading without conflict.
w: HN's go-to answer for shyness and social awkwardness: commenters call it an instruction manual for communicating well and credit it with refocusing how they relate to people.
ab: For people who want practical social skills
Fundamentals still apply despite 1930s examples
Practice matters more than reading alone

q.t: it is the single most useful book I have ever read

t: Philips goLITE BLU Light Therapy Device
s: A compact blue-light therapy lamp with an array of blue LEDs, designed for use in the morning to adjust your sleep cycle and energy.
w: HN sleep-hackers used it for morning blue light to fix insomnia and make themselves early risers, and report it worked better than f.lux, though some balked at the price.
ab: For people with delayed sleep, insomnia, or winter mornings
Small battery-powered unit for morning light exposure
Older discontinued model; pricey

q.t: a few minutes of blue-frequency light every morning turned me into a natural early riser

t: The Shareholder Value Myth: How Putting Shareholders First Harms Investors, Corporations, and the Public
s: A corporate law professor argues that US law does not require maximizing shareholder value and that the idea harms companies and investors.
w: HN commenters cite it when someone claims companies must maximize profit. It is recommended for explaining that directors have no such legal duty.
ab: For readers who want the legal facts behind the profit-first claim
Written in layman terms by a Cornell law professor
Argues a position; the thesis is contested by some

q.t: I highly recommend to just get the book [1], it's written very well and in layman terms

s: A 1970s self-help book on sales and negotiation that argues for projecting success and using takeaway selling.
w: One commenter calls it by far the best sales book he has read, built on the idea that outcomes depend on how intimidated you are. Others read it as a fun, dated cult classic.
ab: For readers curious about old-school sales and negotiation tactics
Advises projecting a strong image before selling
Brash and dated; one commenter jokes about its tone

q.t: Winning Through Intimidation by Robert Ringer is by far the best sales book I ever read.

t: The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy
by: John J. Mearsheimer, Stephen M. Walt
s: A political-science study by two prominent scholars arguing that a pro-Israel lobby has shaped US Middle East policy.
w: Recommended by commenters who want a book-length treatment of how lobbying has shaped US Middle East policy. It is a contested thesis and tends to draw heated threads.
ab: For readers interested in US foreign policy and lobbying
Written by well-known international relations scholars
The central argument is widely disputed

q.t: Israel Lobby and US Foreign Policy by John Mearsheimer. Buy it, read it.

t: Naked Economics: Undressing the Dismal Science
s: A plain-language introduction to economics that explains markets, trade, inflation and policy through everyday examples.
w: The go-to answer on HN when someone asks for the basics of economics: commenters call it intuitive, an overview of how the world works and a book to read if you read nothing else on mainstream econ.
ab: For beginners wanting an intuitive intro to economics
Light, readable, example-driven
Mainstream view; not a deep textbook

q.t: Economics explained in the most intuitive way.

s: A small USB adapter that passes power but blocks data lines, so a charger or port can't read or write to your device.
w: Recommended as the safe 'USB condom' for charging from public ports. One commenter says it has a better case than a bare PCB; another says it is a pain to use always.
ab: For charging in airports and conferences
Passes power only, blocks data
Another thing to carry; some phones need special handling

q.t: There are dongles that only let power through:

t: Effective JavaScript: 68 Specific Ways to Harness the Power of JavaScript
s: A collection of 68 short items explaining how JavaScript really works, in the style of Effective Java and Effective C++.
w: Praised as a favorite intermediate-to-advanced JavaScript book that clarified core language behavior. Commenters note it predates ES6.
ab: For developers who want to understand JavaScript's core
Written for ES5; some advice has changed
Item format, easy to dip into

q.t: I feel like it clarified so many things about Javascript that I didn't have down cold as a self-taught pragmatist.

t: Save the Cat! The Last Book on Screenwriting You'll Ever Need
s: A screenwriting guide that breaks a movie into a set structure of 15 story beats.
w: Commenters call it the most insightful book on movie plot writing, and also cite it to explain why many Hollywood films feel formulaic.
ab: For screenwriters and storytellers
Once read, you notice the beats in many films
Criticized for encouraging formulaic movies

q.t: the most insightful book I've read on that subject

t: Mathematical Proofs: A Transition to Advanced Mathematics
s: Textbook that teaches how to read and write proofs, bridging calculus and abstract mathematics.
w: Suggested as a wonderful book for learning to work through proofs.
ab: For self-learners moving to proof-based math
Exercises included
Textbook style

q.t: started working my way through a wonderful book on mathematical proofs

s: Comprehensive history of cryptography and secret communication from ancient times to the modern era.
w: Called probably the best book in its area, full of stories of cryptographers, though few finish it.
ab: For cryptography and history fans
Very long
Rewarding if you stick with it

q.t: none the less it is an extremely rewarding read.

s: Strang's classic linear algebra textbook, paired with his MIT lectures.
w: HN readers praise Strang as the best way to learn linear algebra for machine learning, with free MIT lectures to match.
ab: For self-learners and ML-bound programmers
Pair it with the MIT OCW lectures
Latest edition is expensive

q.t: Everything I know about linear algebra I learned from this book.

s: A psychiatrist's account of his 1990s clinical research giving DMT to volunteers, and what they experienced.
w: The book HN readers mention when psychedelic research comes up, called a great read on the biology of mystical experiences.
ab: For readers curious about psychedelic research
Based on real clinical trials
Author's speculative claims go beyond the evidence

q.t: The Spirit Molecule was a great read.

s: A guide to software design patterns for games, covering game loops, components, state and more.
w: HN readers still reach for it years later; one commenter pulled it out in 2023 and found it still useful.
ab: For game developers and curious programmers
Clear, funny, well illustrated
Free on the web; this is the print edition

q.t: I pulled it out recently and it still has its usefulnes

s: A question-and-answer introduction to dependent types and proof, in the style of The Little Schemer.
w: HN readers recommend it as a short, great book on proving things about programs, though it is a heavy slog and one calls the writing style impenetrable.
ab: For programmers curious about dependent types and proofs
Playful Socratic Q&A format in the Little series
Divisive style; can be hard going

q.t: two more great, short books on proving things about your program

t: Sprint: How to Solve Big Problems and Test New Ideas in Just Five Days
s: A Google Ventures guide to the five-day design sprint for prototyping and testing product ideas.
w: HN readers treat it as a useful, cool process for concepts and UI/UX projects, and a fundamental outlook on the stages of doing anything. One reader found it just meh.
ab: For product teams that want a structured way to test ideas
Day-by-day process with step instructions
Some find it meh or heavy to run in practice

q.t: is a pretty cool book on working on all kinds of projects, UI/UX projects included

t: Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice
s: Christensen's book on the jobs-to-be-done theory: customers hire products to make progress in a particular circumstance, and innovation should start from that job.
w: Product-minded HN readers cite it as the best explanation of jobs-to-be-done, useful for customer interviews and for thinking about why people actually buy a product.
ab: For product managers, founders, and anyone running customer interviews
You get the jobs-to-be-done framework with company case studies
Business-book style; the core idea is simple and repeated

q.t: models on how to think about innovation

t: The Road Less Traveled: A New Psychology of Love, Traditional Values and Spiritual Growth
s: M. Scott Peck's classic self-help book on discipline, love, growth, and grace, mixing psychotherapy case studies with spiritual reflection.
w: HN commenters call it the best self-improvement book they have read, praising its insight into the human condition and the opening section on discipline. Some read it during hard times.
ab: For readers wanting a thoughtful self-help book on discipline and love
Opening chapters on discipline get the most praise
Contains religious and spiritual themes not everyone wants

q.t: By far the best self-improvement book I've read.

s: The fourth Dune novel, set thousands of years after the original, in which Leto II rules humanity as a tyrant to shape its long-term survival.
w: Fans on HN call it the philosophical peak of the Dune saga, the one that shows humanity across vast stretches of time. Others found it slow and talky.
ab: For readers who have finished the first Dune books
Heavy on philosophy and monologue, light on action
Divides readers; some find it boring

q.t: Work up to it. It's incredibly rewarding.

t: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
s: Jules Verne's 1870 adventure novel about Captain Nemo and his submarine, the Nautilus, told by a professor taken on board.
w: HN commenters cite it as a favorite classic, great fun in a run of Verne books. It shows up in lists of favorite and re-read books.
ab: For readers who enjoy classic adventure and early science fiction
Pick an unabridged modern translation
Nineteenth-century pacing and science; long catalogues of sea life

q.t: Before that I was on a Jules Verne kick

s: 14-inch business laptop from 2013 with a swappable battery, a TrackPoint, upgradeable memory and storage, and a user-replaceable internal design.
w: HN developers recommended it as a cheap, sturdy Linux laptop with a great keyboard and long battery life, and the last T-series where you can replace nearly every part yourself.
ab: For Linux users wanting a cheap, repairable used laptop
Swappable battery, TrackPoint, upgradeable RAM and storage
Old hardware, and the Synaptics touchpad needs configuring

q.t: Built like a tank, ~12 hour battery life, great keyboard, every thing just works under linux

s: Polish fantasy series about Geralt of Rivia, a monster hunter, following him through short stories and a five-novel saga.
w: Polish speakers on HN call it the best fiction they have read, and other readers came to the books through the Witcher 3 game and read them all quickly. One says it reads best in the original Polish.
ab: For fantasy readers, including fans of the games and shows
Start with the short story collections
Translation quality is debated; some say the Polish original reads better

q.t: This was the best fiction book I've ever read.

s: McCullough's biography of Wilbur and Orville Wright and their path to the first controlled, powered flight.
w: HN readers praise it as an easy, hard-to-put-down biography that shows how persistence and logical thinking paid off, and explains what it took to make flight happen.
ab: For readers who like engineering and invention stories
Easy, narrative biography
Popular history rather than technical detail

q.t: wonderful book on the Wright Brothers, easy to read, shows that persistence and logic thinking pays out

s: A developer-focused HP laptop with an AMD Ryzen processor that shipped with System76's Pop!_OS Linux preinstalled and upgradeable memory.
w: Commenters recommend it as a mainstream-brand laptop that runs Linux out of the box, citing good reviews and easy RAM upgrades to 64GB.
ab: For developers wanting preinstalled Linux from a big brand
RAM can be upgraded, one owner went to 64GB
Limited availability; an older generation of hardware now

q.t: all of the reviews have been phenomenal

s: A book on how network-effect products launch and scale, drawing on Uber, Tinder and Dropbox, by an Andreessen Horowitz partner.
w: Founders of networked products praise it as a rare business book that is not self-aggrandising, with real depth on scaling at Uber. One commenter has re-read it three times.
ab: For founders building marketplaces or social products
Covers launching a network, scaling and defensibility
Less relevant if your product has no network effects

q.t: I have re-read that book 3 times now, its that good

s: Mark Twain's 1884 novel following a boy and an escaped slave on a raft down the Mississippi.
w: HN readers include it in must-read lists and favorites, praising the vivid voice that puts you in its world.
ab: American classic with distinctive vernacular narration.
Public domain, free in many editions.
Contains period language and themes.

q.t: One of the most vividly written books I read.

s: Simak's 1952 linked stories about a far-future Earth where dogs and robots inherit the planet after humanity leaves.
w: HN sci-fi readers recommend it often as a lesser-known favorite.
ab: Classic pastoral sci-fi.
Short linked stories.
Gentle, older style.

s: A self-help workbook that takes readers from basic algebra up to first-semester calculus, with quizzes and exercises.
w: The pick for adults relearning math from scratch. Commenters say it is clear, has many exercises, and builds from fractions toward calculus.
ab: For adults or students relearning math from the basics
Short quiz opens each chapter
Covers up to first-semester calculus only

q.t: She basically starts out with the simplest algebra (fractions) and gradually works up to topics in 1st semester Calculus.

t: Smart & Gets Things Done: Joel Spolsky's Concise Guide to Finding the Best Technical Talent
s: Joel Spolsky's short guide to hiring great software developers, expanding on his Guerrilla Guide to Interviewing.
w: The book people point to when talking about hiring programmers, as a compact expansion of Spolsky's interviewing essays.
ab: For managers and founders hiring developers
Short and opinionated
Some advice shows 2000s-era practices

q.t: I just bought Smart and Gets Things Done by Joel Spolsky on hiring the best programmers.

s: A guide to estimating and planning software projects with story points, velocity and release planning.
w: Recommended in estimation threads as probably the best resource on the problem, with its coverage of relative estimation and story points.
ab: For developers and managers who plan and estimate
Covers story points, velocity and release planning
Published in 2005; some agile practices have evolved

q.t: Mike Cohn's work in AEAP is thorough and worthwhile and probably still the best resource for solving the problem of estimation

t: 747: Creating the World's First Jumbo Jet and Other Adventures from a Life in Aviation
s: The memoir of the engineer who led the design of the Boeing 747, covering the program and a career in aviation.
w: Commenters recommend it for the inside story of how the 747 was designed, and for its discussion of redundancy, safety and testing.
ab: For engineering and aviation history fans
Insider account of a huge program
Memoir, so one engineer's perspective

q.t: Would highly recommend this book by Joe Sutter the engineering leader for the 747 program

t: Peter Norton's Assembly Language Book for the IBM PC
s: A 1980s introduction to 8086 assembly programming on the IBM PC, building a disk editor along the way.
w: Fondly remembered as a simple, hands-on way into assembly. Commenters say it is archaic but teaches by building a real disk-editing tool.
ab: For nostalgic or curious learners of x86 basics
DOS-era 16-bit code, not modern assembly
Teaches by building a working utility

q.t: It goes through lessons that build up to a pretty good interactive disk editor (DSKPATCH) written entirely in x86 assembly.

t: The Great Influenza: The Story of the Deadliest Pandemic in History
s: A history of the 1918 influenza pandemic and of the rise of scientific medicine in America.
w: Recommended repeatedly during COVID discussions as a gripping account that also traces the history of medicine. Commenters say COVID is not a good model for 1918.
ab: For readers interested in pandemics and medical history
Narrative history with scientific detail
1918 flu was far more lethal than COVID

q.t: Great book about this (and, more broadly, the rise of medicine as a scientific endeavor)

s: A short ebook on using pre-commitment, rewards and goal systems to motivate yourself.
w: Recommended to people who can't finish projects, with one reader saying it was the book that shaped their year.
ab: Practical motivation tactics
Cheap ebook
Author's personal experiments

q.t: Great read, teaches you how to motivate yourself to get shit done.

s: Interviews and stories from the people behind interaction design, collected by the IDEO co-founder who designed the first laptop.
w: Recommended to developers who want to get better at design, as a book about how users interact with products beyond web pages. One wishes for a revised edition.
ab: For developers and designers learning interaction design
Interviews with pioneers, with many photos and examples
Published in 2007; later technology is not covered

q.t: they helped me understand how users interact with my user interfaces

t: You Can't Teach a Kid to Ride a Bike at a Seminar
s: The Sandler Selling System's seven-step approach to consultative selling, from qualifying prospects to closing.
w: Recommended in threads about learning to sell as the best sales book some commenters have seen, with one using its ideas daily. Others took a Sandler class.
ab: For founders and engineers who need to learn sales
A seven-step system for qualifying and closing
Methodology is a bit salesy and dated

q.t: The book is cheap and an excellent read.

s: A book on designing fast networked devices, covering algorithms and architecture for routers, switches and protocol implementations.
w: tptacek calls it the book on high-performance network component design, and other commenters put it on lists of awesome, mildly impractical systems books.
ab: For engineers building high-speed networking software or hardware
Cross-layer techniques from hardware to algorithms
Specialized and dated in places (2005)

q.t: Varghese, a co-author on the ACM paper, wrote the book on high-performance network component design

t: The Happiness Advantage: The Seven Principles of Positive Psychology That Fuel Success and Performance at Work
s: A book arguing that positive psychology habits lead to better work performance, with seven principles including the 20-second rule.
w: Recommended for being based on studies and for the 20-second rule on lowering activation energy. One commenter says it helped a relative.
ab: For readers wanting science-based self-improvement
Seven principles with practical exercises
Positive-psychology claims have seen replication questions

q.t: I'd also recommend the Happiness Advantage

s: Argues that parenting style has less long-term effect on children's personalities than genes and peer groups.
w: Recommended as a book-length look at research showing genetics and peers matter more than parenting style.
ab: For parents and psychology readers
Provocative thesis
Parts of the research may be dated

q.t: I highly recommend this book-length treatment of the research literature

s: Dawkins presents the evidence for evolution by natural selection.
w: Cited as a reference for evidence of evolution and recommended to skeptics.
ab: For evolution skeptics and learners
Evidence-focused
Popular science style

q.t: Strongly recommend you read Dawkins' "The Greatest Show on Earth"

s: Knuth's fully documented source code for TeX in literate-programming style, with commentary on every part of the program.
w: Recommended as a model of exposition for a large program; commenters learned a lot from reading it even though it is written in a 1970s style.
ab: For readers who want to study a classic codebase
Literate programming in Pascal/WEB
Very dated style; long and dense

q.t: TeX: The Program is still a fascinating read because of the exceptional attention that Knuth has paid to exposition

t: I Could Tell You But Then You Would Have to Be Destroyed By Me
s: A collection of military black-program patches by Trevor Paglen.
w: Recommended as a Paglen classic on secret program emblems.
ab: For fans of secrecy and military culture.
Photographic collection.
Niche.

q.t: Another Paglen classic, which I highly recommend to anyone interested in this sort of thing

t: The World of Mathematics: A Four-Volume Set
s: A four-volume Dover anthology of essays and original source writings on mathematics, from history to applications, by many authors.
w: HN recommends the set for original source material, a big mix of essays that is fabulous and cheap used. One reader warns it has little math proper or depth.
ab: For browsing math history and culture
Four volumes of essays by many authors
Little technical depth; essays are mid-century

q.t: For original source material (more essays than papers, but a pretty big mix of stuff), this set is fabulous
