w: HN names it as one of the most recommended books for learning C and C++ memory when coming from high-level languages. Reviews are stellar, though the book is pricey.
ab: For high-level programmers learning how memory really works
Concise and focused on pitfalls and debugging
Expensive; the library is a good first stop

q.t: A rather expensive book but stellar reviews.

s: A low-priced Dover introduction to graph theory covering paths, trees, connectivity, planarity and colorings, with many worked examples and exercises.
w: HN names it as a good basic graph theory book at a Dover price. One reader enjoys it but warns it is fairly beginner-level if you already like math.
ab: For self-learners meeting graph theory for the first time
Cheap Dover paperback with many exercises
Elementary; math-savvy readers will want a more thorough text

q.t: quite enjoy it, although it's fairly beginner if you're a math person

s: An introductory machine-learning textbook that teaches the main algorithms with working Python code and light mathematics.
w: HN recommends it as a less math-heavy machine-learning book. It lacks the proofs of heavier texts, but the code gets you started on basic data analysis.
ab: For programmers who want ML with code before theory
Python examples using numpy
2009 edition; modern deep learning not covered

q.t: the code is decent and will get you started doing some basic data analysis

s: An 8-inch stamped stainless-steel chef's knife with a textured nonslip handle, made by Victorinox in Switzerland.
w: HN's go-to budget kitchen knife: Cook's Illustrated's top pick at about $30, used so heavily by butchers that it wears into a boning knife.
ab: For cooks who want a great knife without the price
Grippy handle, light, easy to sharpen
Plain looks; softer steel than pricier knives

q.t: The top rated chef's knife by Cook's Illustrated is only about $30 (and it's awesome)

by: James W. Heisig, Timothy W. Richardson
s: A mnemonic method for learning the meaning and writing of traditional Chinese characters through imaginative stories built from component parts.
w: HN learners suggest Heisig's method as a structured way to memorize characters. They say it builds intuition for unfamiliar characters and beats a year of casual app study.
ab: For learners who want to write traditional characters
Teaches meaning and writing, not pronunciation
Rote story-making is divisive among Chinese learners

q.t: The Japanese version of this book is quite well-known and I found it helpful

by: James W. Heisig, Timothy W. Richardson
s: A mnemonic method for learning the meaning and writing of simplified Chinese characters through imaginative stories built from component parts.
w: HN learners use it for characters alongside a vocabulary app, finding Chinese easier than expected. Another commenter says it beats casual app study for reading characters.
ab: For learners who want to read and write simplified characters
Teaches meaning and writing, not pronunciation
Pair with a vocabulary tool for words

q.t: I find it a lot easier than I initially thought it would be

t: Understanding Unix/Linux Programming: A Guide to Theory and Practice
s: A systems-programming text that teaches the Unix API by rebuilding common commands such as who, tail and ls from scratch in C.
w: Praised on HN for diving into how Linux works through deconstructing familiar commands, and as a good starter before the heavier Richard Stevens books.
ab: For C programmers learning Unix systems programming
Learn by rewriting standard Unix tools
Aimed at beginners; Stevens covers the deeper material

q.t: I found it quite inspiring as to where to spend time while learning UNIX.

s: A vertical, joystick-style ergonomic mouse that keeps the hand in a handshake position, sold in small/medium and large sizes.
w: HN sufferers of RSI and carpal tunnel say it fixed their problem after trying other pointing devices, though it feels like a joystick rather than a mouse.
ab: For people with wrist, hand or carpal tunnel pain
Vertical grip; sizes available
Takes getting used to; the feel is joystick-like

q.t: but ultimately, a new mouse is what was the best solution for me.

s: A practical guide to designing logos and lettering, covering alphabet construction, typefaces, symbols and drawing technique, with many examples.
w: HN recommends it in design and typography learning lists and as a gift for designers, praised as a no-nonsense book with zero fluff and plenty of information per page.
ab: For designers learning logo and lettering craft
Dense visual reference with how-to sections
Print-era examples; software tips are dated

q.t: with absolutely zero fluff and maximum good information per page.

t: Ordering Disorder: Grid Principles for Web Design
s: A designer's guide to applying typographic grid systems to web layouts, by the former design director of the New York Times website.
w: Cited in lists for learning grids and layout on the web, and called a good book focused entirely on web design, though Brockmann's classic is seen as the deeper reference.
ab: For web designers and front-end developers learning layout grids
Web-specific, unlike classic print grid books
Written in 2011, so responsive design coverage is thin

q.t: Khoi Vinh's Ordering Disorder is a good book on grids, and its focused entirely on web design.

t: Negotiating Your Salary: How to Make $1000 a Minute
s: A short guide to salary negotiation with scripts for common questions, counter-offers and objections.

ab: For employees negotiating job offers or raises
Includes example questions, answers and counters
Sensational title; advice is general, not tech specific

q.t: I can attest to increasing my income by tens of thousands of dollars by putting its ideas into practice.

t: Copycats: How Smart Companies Use Imitation to Gain a Strategic Edge
s: A business school look at why imitation often beats innovation and how companies can copy and improve successfully.
w: Recommended on HN whenever founders obsess over novelty. Commenters use it to argue that fast followers who execute better often win.
ab: For founders and strategists weighing innovating versus copying
Case studies of successful imitators
Academic style

q.t: There's a fantastic book on this

s: A compact tutorial on Bayesian methods for data analysis, aimed at scientists and engineers.
w: HN recommends it as an excellent hands-on introduction to Bayesian reasoning, and as a companion to Jaynes. One reader says it suits anyone fluent with calculus.
ab: For scientists and engineers who want practical Bayesian analysis
Short and accessible with worked examples
Needs comfort with calculus

q.t: Not articles but there are two very excellent books on the subject that I can't recommend enough:

s: A technical introduction to the statistics and modeling of high-frequency financial data and market microstructure.
w: Recommended by HN quants as the real reference on high-frequency trading, and for time series techniques that apply well beyond finance.
ab: For quantitative people wanting a technical grounding in HFT
Covers time series and market data analysis
Math-heavy and academic

q.t: the techniques covered in the book are generic enough to apply to all kinds of time series

s: A guide to measuring and acting on website data, with an emphasis on customer outcomes over raw traffic metrics.
w: HN's recommendation for getting started in analytics. Commenters say Kaushik's books are full of best practices.

Explains what to measure and why
Tool details have changed since 2010

q.t: They are highly recommended and full of best practices that you should be aware of.

t: Reality Is Broken: Why Games Make Us Better and How They Can Change the World
s: Game designer Jane McGonigal argues that game mechanics can make real life more engaging and solve real problems.
w: Recommended on HN for understanding why games motivate and how flow works. Commenters bring it up on gamification and why work can feel fun.
ab: For game designers and product people interested in motivation
Makes the case for gameplay in everyday life
Optimistic; some claims are overreaching

q.t: I recommend this book and audiobook about gammification to understand flow better.

t: Don't Shoot the Dog! The New Art of Teaching and Training
s: Animal trainer Karen Pryor explains positive reinforcement and behavior shaping, for pets, children, coworkers and yourself.
w: HN recommends it on conditioning and behavior change, noting that positive reinforcement beats punishment. One reader says it was unusually good for popular nonfiction.
ab: For pet owners, parents and managers
Explains positive reinforcement and shaping
Animal-training examples dominate

q.t: I found this book unusually good for a popular nonfiction book

s: A large trackball made by Microsoft around 2000, discontinued and now only available used at high prices.

ab: For trackball fans who want a cult classic
Hard to find; used prices are very high
Optical but old, USB/PS2 era

q.t: The single most awesome input device ever designed.

s: A guide to clear business writing, from emails and memos to proposals and speeches, by two former Ogilvy executives.
w: HN's favorite on business writing, recommended to people moving into leadership. Commenters say it made their emails crisper.
ab: For professionals who write emails, memos and reports
Short, practical advice
Corporate focus, dated examples

q.t: My favorite book on writing comes from advertising.

t: Think Like a Programmer: An Introduction to Creative Problem Solving
s: A book teaching programming problem solving through exercises, rather than the syntax of a particular language.
w: HN recommends it to beginners and teachers as a way to learn problem solving. Commenters call it helpful and say it is hard to come by otherwise.
ab: For beginners stuck on how to approach problems
Exercise-based and language-agnostic in spirit
C++ examples

q.t: and I find it quite helpful

s: The first five Silo novellas collected in one volume: a post-apocalyptic story of people living in an underground silo whose rules nobody may question.
w: HN readers list it among their best reads of the year, noting it began as self-published Kindle singles and that the first installment is free to try.
ab: For readers who like dystopian, closed-world science fiction
Collects the first five Silo stories in one ebook
Series continues past this omnibus; first part is free to sample

q.t: It ranks among the best zero dollars I spent

t: Luxe Bidet Neo 120 Non-Electric Mechanical Bidet Attachment
s: A non-electric, cold-water bidet attachment that fits under a standard toilet seat and uses a spring-loaded retractable nozzle.
w: HN commenters suggest it as the cheap alternative to a heated Japanese toilet seat. Owners say it gets the job done for about $35.
ab: For anyone who wants a bidet without electricity
Installs under the existing seat
Water is at pipe temperature, not heated

q.t: I own one, and I highly recommend them.

t: Just My Type: A Book About Fonts
s: A lively history of typefaces, their designers and their stories, with chapters on well-known fonts.
w: HN commenters recommend it as a fun, anecdotal introduction to typefaces for people who want appreciation more than a how-to manual.
ab: For readers curious about type history
History and anecdotes, not practical typography rules
Good for building appreciation of fonts

q.t: I find it quite a fun read, and it can inspire your interests and appreciation for types, if you don't already know much about typography.

t: Write Great Code, Volume 1: Understanding the Machine
s: Explains how CPUs, memory, data representation and compilers work so programmers can write more efficient high-level code.
w: HN commenters include it among books for learning how computers work below the language level and for programmers wanting to understand the machine.
ab: For programmers wanting low-level machine knowledge
Language-agnostic orientation
Hardware examples are somewhat dated

s: A British journalist reads his own Stasi file after reunification and tracks down the informants who reported on him.
w: HN commenters recommend it as a personal account of East German surveillance, especially readers who want the human stories of informants.
ab: For readers interested in the Stasi and surveillance
Memoir that doubles as investigation
Pairs well with Stasiland

t: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites
s: A highly visual beginner's guide to HTML and CSS with a photographic layout and one topic per page spread.
w: HN commenters recommend it for beginners who want a clear visual overview of web basics and a beautiful book to learn from.
ab: For beginners learning HTML and CSS
Visual, spread-per-topic design
Does not cover modern CSS layout much

q.t: I would recommend getting this beautiful book by Jon Duckett that covers both the design and development basics for a website

t: The Cleanest Race: How North Koreans See Themselves and Why It Matters
s: An analysis of North Korean propaganda arguing that the regime is driven by race-based nationalism rather than Marxism.
w: HN commenters recommend it for a different view of how North Koreans see themselves, citing its racial-nationalist reading of the regime.
ab: For readers curious about North Korean ideology
Based on analysis of propaganda texts
Its thesis is debated among scholars

q.t: I find this book to open a new perspective on the way north korean people see themselves and their leaders.

s: A collection of Borges's essays, reviews and lectures, including A New Refutation of Time and Pascal's Sphere.

ab: For readers who have finished Borges's fiction
Essays on literature, time and ideas
Best after reading his stories

q.t: Borges is most widely read for his fiction, but his Selected Non-Fictions[1] is life altering.

s: A short ebook explaining stock options and equity compensation, exercising and tax implications for startup employees.

ab: For startup employees evaluating equity
Short and plain-spoken

t: Joe Celko's Thinking in Sets: Auxiliary, Temporal, and Virtual Tables in SQL

Celko's style is opinionated

t: Cherry MX Rubber O-Ring Switch Dampeners

w: Used by mechanical keyboard fans to cut noise; one says they do not affect feel much but reduce the sound substantially.

Cheap and easy to fit
Feel effect varies by person

s: A home cold brew coffee maker using a plastic brewing bucket, felt filter and glass carafe.

ab: For cold brew drinkers at home
Reusable filters last about ten batches each
Bulky plastic bucket

q.t: I have a toddy, produces excellent quality cold brew.

t: Jeffrey Gitomer's Little Red Book of Selling
s: A short sales book of principles for prospecting, networking and winning customers.

ab: For people new to sales
Short and motivational
Old-school sales style

t: Love Yourself Like Your Life Depends on It
s: A short book on practicing self-love as a daily habit, written after the author's depression.

Very short and personal
Light on evidence

Case histories from civil engineering
Mostly bridges and structures

t: The Fortune Cookie Chronicles: Adventures in the World of Chinese Food
s: A journalist traces the history and culture of Chinese food in America.

Journalistic and fun
US-focused

t: The Search for the Perfect Language
s: Eco's history of centuries of attempts to design or rediscover a perfect, universal language.

s: A plain-language primer on reading financial statements for non-finance managers.

Short and plain-English
Basic coverage; not a deep accounting text

s: A former Microsoft Research director argues that technology amplifies human intent but can't fix social problems by itself.

Case-study driven, quick read

t: How to Talk About Books You Haven't Read

Vegan, low-fat approach
Contested science; consult a doctor

Tiny, cheap, with microSD slot
Basic features and plastic build

A textbook with problem sets

Not a first encounter with proofs

Instruction-set focused

ab: For readers who want the formal mathematics of AGI

q.t: I highly recommend Markus Hutter's book

s: A high-school geometry text by the Russian mathematician Gelfand, completed by colleagues and published in English by Springer in 2020.

Problem-driven and demanding

q.t: israel gelfand, a top russian mathematician, has books aimed at high school students

Simplified; not a guide to production systems

s: A history of Central Asia from 800 to 1200, covering its scientists, scholars and cities before the Mongol conquest.

s: A critique of measurement obsession in organizations, with case studies from education, medicine, policing and business.
w: Offered as a counterweight to data-driven everything: HN readers say it gives a detailed account of when metrics succeed and when they backfire.

Case studies across schools, hospitals, police and firms
Argument is one-sided at times

q.t: Found it to be an interesting read

t: Designing Distributed Systems: Patterns and Paradigms for Scalable, Reliable Services
s: A short book of reusable patterns, such as sidecars, ambassadors and scatter-gather, for building distributed systems on containers.
w: HN suggests it as a high-level pattern book when people ask about learning distributed systems.

Light on theory

Emphasizes style, comments and debugging

Test-driven chapters

t: Fluent C: Principles, Practices, and Patterns
s: A patterns book for C programmers on error handling, memory, API design and code organisation.
w: Offered in Ask HN threads on learning C, praised for its structure and for covering design concerns in C.
ab: For programmers who already know C basics
Pattern format
New, with few reviews

t: AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models
s: A book on building real applications with foundation models, covering evaluation, prompting, RAG, finetuning and deployment.
w: Listed among textbooks recommended to AI engineers; one commenter says it inspired a side project.

Covers evaluation and production concerns
Field moves fast, so details may age

Dated web techniques

q.t: I just started reading "Web Design for Developers" published by PragProg

Covers RSpec and Cucumber
Old versions of the tools

ab: For job-seeking programmers
Practical advice on resumes and interviews
Dated: the job market has changed

Covers exercise, diet and workspace
Some research is older

q.t: You should read the book The healthy programmer by  Joe Kutner.

s: A tour of Ruby's object model and metaprogramming, with a fictional pair-programming story.

ab: For Rubyists who want to understand the object model
Story-driven
Covers Ruby 2.x

t: Seven More Languages in Seven Weeks
s: A tour of Lua, Factor, Elm, Elixir, Julia, miniKanren and Idris, with a chapter each.
w: Recommended as a follow-up to Seven Languages in Seven Weeks, for learning how different languages think.
ab: For programmers who want to broaden their view
Seven languages, light introductions
Language versions have moved on

q.t: they're a whole lot of fun

w: Recommended for learning Ecto, with a chapter on application design and contexts.
ab: For Elixir developers using databases
Covers queries and changesets
Tied to Ecto 3-era APIs

q.t: Also Programming Ecto is great.

s: A Pragmatic Bookshelf guide to machine learning with Elixir's Nx, Axon and Livebook.
w: Recommended by commenters who say Elixir has become good at machine learning, with clear writing and many examples.
ab: For Elixir developers interested in ML
Many examples
Niche ecosystem

s: A Manning guide to building web applications and web services in Go, from server-rendered pages through to REST APIs.

Covers server-rendered views, then a full section on web services
Written for older Go versions; check framework choices

by: David A. Black, Joseph Leo III

ab: For programmers who want Ruby, not just Rails
Third edition targets Ruby 2.5
Newer Ruby releases postdate it

q.t: It's been kept up to date (3rd edition was released in 2019)

s: A beginner-oriented Haskell book organized as a series of short lessons, each building on the previous one.
w: Regularly named in Haskell learning threads as a gentle starting point. People like the small lessons that stack up and make the language's ideas click.
ab: For beginners to Haskell and functional programming
Short lessons with capstone-style projects
Pair with a deeper book once the basics click

q.t: Made up of small lessons that all build on top of each other and will really help you understand what's going on.

s: An intermediate Haskell book covering practical topics such as type-level features, concurrency, testing and project structure through worked examples.
w: Recommended as the next step after the basics and praised as brilliant for learning Haskell through small projects.
ab: For people who already know Haskell basics
Project-driven chapters on real-world topics
Not an introduction for absolute beginners

q.t: This one is nothing short of brilliant:

s: A book on modeling data and controlling complexity in Java using records, sealed types and pattern matching.

Starts with basic examples and builds up
Ideas apply beyond Java

t: The Manga Guide to Linear Algebra

Story-driven with worked examples
Not a substitute for a full textbook

q.t: Obligatory plug for the Manga Guide to Linear Algebra

s: A comic-format introduction to cryptography covering ciphers, public-key ideas and hashing through a story.

Manga format with explanations
Introductory only

q.t: The Manga Guide to Cryptography came out recently, if that's more your style

s: A fast-paced, project-driven introduction to modern C++ covering C++17 features for people who already program.

ab: For programmers wanting modern C++ quickly
Covers C++17
Newer standards not covered

t: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 2nd Edition
s: A beginner Python book that teaches practical scripting for spreadsheets, files, PDFs, web scraping and email.

ab: For non-programmers and beginners
Task-focused projects like spreadsheets and PDFs
Light on theory and software design

q.t: a popular recommendation of mine for those who want to learn what it looks like while having a decent introduction

s: A history of Chile's Project Cybersyn, Salvador Allende's attempt to manage the economy with cybernetics and computers.

Scholarly tone

Broad overview across subjects
Brisk pace

Classical methods, not deep learning

t: Spreadsheet Implementation Technology: Basics and Extensions
s: A MIT Press book by Peter Sestoft on how spreadsheets are built, covering formula evaluation, recalculation, dependencies and implementation techniques.

Predates dynamic-array functions like SORT and UNIQUE

q.t: There is not a lot of literature on spreadsheet implementation

s: Apple's streaming box for TVs with a clean interface, app store and support for Dolby Vision and Atmos.

ab: For people who want a clean, ad-free streaming interface on any TV
Supports Dolby Vision and Atmos in newer models
Costs more than other streaming sticks

s: Wired over-ear noise-cancelling headphones from Bose that run on a replaceable AAA battery.

Replaceable AAA battery and ear cushions

Comic format with economics and ethics arguments

Ships with Ubuntu; slim, light build
Newer generations criticized; fan noise noted

Battery life is modest; some report driver issues

q.t: great luck with the Thinkpad P14s range with AMD CPUs

s: A line of robot vacuum cleaners from iRobot that clean floors on a schedule or from an app.

ab: For retro computing fans
History of the Amiga platform
Part of a platform series

ab: For readers curious about how the US government works

s: A business parable in which a mentor teaches a young man 23 profit models.

Examples from early 2000s

Interview format; easy to dip into
Rooted in 1970s America

Weaker standalone value

s: A 1994 prison drama directed by Frank Darabont, based on a Stephen King novella, about an innocent banker's friendship and long escape plan.

ab: For anyone who wants a classic, hopeful drama

q.t: Shawshank Redemption: "Never ever ever ever ever give up"!

t: Differentiate or Die: Survival in Our Era of Killer Competition

ab: For founders learning marketing differentiation and branding basics
Same school as Positioning, by Jack Trout
Early 2000s examples; mentions are mostly list entries

t: The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying

ab: For readers exploring Buddhism, meditation and mortality
Practical meditation guidance and teachings on death

ab: For true-crime fans, especially those interested in tech-adjacent crime
Narrative reporting on Paul Le Roux's rise and arrest
Violent, dark subject matter

t: Harmonic Experience: Tonal Harmony from Its Natural Origins to Its Modern Expression
s: A music theory book that teaches harmony by singing against a drone and building from the overtone series.
w: Recommended as a natural, experiential way into western tonal harmony, though pricey as a first book.
ab: Teaches harmony by ear and singing
Starts with overtones
Expensive and unconventional

t: Life at the Bottom: The Worldview That Makes the Underclass
s: Essays by a prison doctor on the culture of the British underclass.
w: Recommended for insight into the mindset around poverty, though it is a contested conservative view.
ab: For readers exploring poverty and culture.
Essays from a doctor in a slum hospital.
Politically contested.

q.t: He's British psychologist who spent his life working with the poor, and came away with some insightful observations

s: Marcus Aurelius' private notes on Stoic practice, in Gregory Hays' modern translation.
w: Recommended specifically for the Hays translation, which avoids archaic English.
ab: For readers new to Stoicism.
Modern, readable translation.
Short entries.

q.t: I recommend Gregory Hays' new translation, without the 'thou's and 'dost's.

t: Linear Algebra and Learning from Data
s: Gilbert Strang's textbook linking linear algebra to machine learning.
w: Recommended for conversational but terse treatment with ML applications.
ab: For learners with some linear algebra.
Companion to MIT course.
Terse.

q.t: I think the pacing and exercises in the above Strang book are great.

t: Analog Circuit Design: Art, Science, and Personalities
s: A collection of essays by analog designers.
w: Called a favorite circuit book, written in an approachable way.
ab: For electronics hobbyists.
Essays.

q.t: It is written from zen-level experts in a very ELI5 way.

t: Enchantment: The Art of Changing Hearts, Minds, and Actions
s: A book on how to win people over through likability, trustworthiness and a great cause, from a former Apple evangelist.
w: HN readers put it on their best-of-year lists and like Kawasaki's practical, less tech-focused take on persuading people.

Some tips feel dated now

q.t: I like Guy Kawasaki's books. This one is a bit less focused on startup/tech

Step-by-step intro for Objective-C beginners
Obsolete: Objective-C and the iOS SDK have changed a lot

s: A line of e-ink e-readers Sony sold from 2006 to the mid-2010s, since discontinued.

ab: Historical interest: discontinued e-ink readers
Reads DRM-free ebooks
Available only used

s: A durable plastic fountain pen with a triangular grip, widely used as a first fountain pen.
w: Mentioned by HN users as an affordable, nice-to-write-with starter fountain pen.
ab: For beginners curious about fountain pens
Cheap for a fountain pen
Triangular grip not for everyone

q.t: I got a LAMY safari and it's so nice to write with.

t: Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness
by: Richard H. Thaler & Cass R. Sunstein

ab: For readers curious about behavioral economics and design defaults
Origin of the nudge concept
Some HN readers dislike its paternalism

q.t: cites one of the best nudges ever introduced - automatic enrollment in retirement savings plans.

Late-1990s style.

Provocative thesis, politically charged
Some HN recommenders have only read about it

CBT-style, drug-free six-week program

ab: For students entering proof-based math
Companion style
Short chapters

Counterpoint to revisionists

Contested

q.t: it walks through the process of creating a quite complex game and has some useful recipes and examples.

s: A rigorous text on deriving programs from specifications using category theory and the calculus of relations, in a functional setting.

ab: For readers comfortable with category theory and functional programming

t: A Geometry of Music: Harmony and Counterpoint in the Extended Common Practice

ab: For mathematically inclined musicians and curious programmers
Treats harmony as geometry across many genres
Academic in tone and demanding in places

q.t: I learned about that book here on HN from another participant.

t: Why Men Earn More: The Startling Truth Behind the Pay Gap
s: A book arguing that the gender pay gap largely reflects differing life and career choices rather than discrimination.
w: HN commenters bring it up in pay-gap debates as a book that explains the gap through choices. It is contested and used as a polemical reference.
ab: For readers following the pay gap debate
Argues choices and trade-offs explain the gap
Controversial; critics dispute its conclusions

q.t: The pay difference is a matter of a multitude of life choices made slightly differently between men and women.

s: A 10-inch netbook with a Loongson MIPS processor, known for running fully free software.
w: HN knows it as Richard Stallman's laptop, and free-software fans keep asking where to buy one. Commenters note it is slow but works with fully free firmware.
ab: For free-software purists and curiosity buyers
Runs without proprietary firmware
Slow, old hardware

q.t: I've wanted to purchase a Leemote laptop/computer for a while now

s: A textbook on functional programming that teaches program reasoning and equational proofs, using a Haskell-like notation.
w: HN lists it among the books for learning functional programming and reasoning about algorithms. Commenters pair it with SICP and Programming in Haskell.
ab: For people wanting a rigorous functional programming foundation
Emphasizes reasoning about programs
Older notation, not a modern Haskell tutorial

q.t: here are the books which I highly suggest everyone to read:

s: A split, curved ergonomic keyboard with a wrist rest, produced by Microsoft in the late 1990s and 2000s.
w: HN typists defend it as a comfortable split design and a low-cost pick. Some call it the best keyboard created and say few have improved on it.
ab: For typists wanting a split ergonomic layout
Inexpensive and comfortable for many
Old membrane keys; buy used or alternatives

q.t: Split enough for ergonomics, good key response, not very expensive.

t: Beginning iOS 5 Development: Exploring the iOS SDK
s: A beginner's guide to building iPhone and iPad apps with the iOS 5 SDK and Objective-C.
w: Mentioned on HN as a useful way to start iOS development back in 2011-2012. It's tied to old iOS and Objective-C.
ab: For beginners in the iOS 5 era
Walks through building sample apps
Obsolete: Objective-C and iOS 5 are long outdated

q.t: I found this one very useful to get started

t: Catching Fire: How Cooking Made Us Human

w: Cited on HN when new evidence on early fire use appears. One commenter says it makes the case against raw diets very well.
ab: For readers curious about human evolution and diet
Argues cooking shaped our biology
Hypothesis is contested

q.t: this books makes the case against raw diets very well

t: Between Silk and Cyanide: A Codemaker's War, 1941-1945
s: Memoir of the head of codes at Britain's Special Operations Executive, who fought to give agents better ciphers in occupied Europe.
w: HN readers recommend it as a first-hand account of wartime cryptography, including the story of using silk instead of paper for codes.
ab: For readers of cryptography and WWII history
Insider account of SOE codemaking
Memoir with wartime drama and bureaucratic fights

q.t: I recently read Between Silk and Cyanide, the autobiography of the guy who made the codes

t: Currency Wars: The Making of the Next Global Crisis
s: A popular account of currency conflicts and monetary policy, arguing that currency manipulation and a shift toward SDRs threaten the dollar system.
w: HN commenters mention it as a fascinating read on yuan, dollar and reserve-currency fights, though mostly as something on their reading list.
ab: For readers following currency and reserve-currency debates
Author takes a bearish, gold-friendly view
Predictions from 2011 have not all aged well

q.t: I read a fascinating book on the topic.

s: A programmable toy tank that takes a sequence of keypad commands, a modern re-release of the 1979 original.
w: HN commenters remember it as an early introduction to programming for children and suggest the newer version for kids learning to code.
ab: For kids and nostalgic adults learning sequencing
Programmed with a simple keypad
Not identical to the original 1980s version

q.t: I've often thought of getting the newer version for my daughter

t: The Imp of the Mind: Exploring the Silent Epidemic of Obsessive Bad Thoughts
s: A self-help book by an OCD specialist about unwanted intrusive thoughts, explaining that they are common and how cognitive-behavioral techniques treat them.
w: HN commenters recommend it to people troubled by intrusive thoughts, and a clinician calls it a favorite book for patients.
ab: For readers troubled by intrusive or obsessive thoughts
Written by a clinician specializing in OCD
Science is somewhat dated, per one clinician

q.t: my favorite book for patients is this one by Lee Baer, a bit outdated on the science but the clinical discussion is right on

t: Flents Quiet Please Foam Ear Plugs (50 Pair)
s: Cylindrical soft foam earplugs sold in a box of 50 pairs.
w: HN commenters use them for noise blocking, on their own or under earmuffs, and one says full-size cylindrical foam works best for sleeping with larger ear canals.
ab: For sleeping or concentrating in noisy places
Cylindrical shape suits larger ear canals
Disposable foam, replace regularly

q.t: much more comfortable to wear than the earmuffs I had worn previously. Several hours is no problem.

s: A budget Windows Phone 8 smartphone sold unlocked and prepaid on AT&T for around $50 to $70.
w: HN commenters recommended it as a very cheap backup phone that works fine for its price, despite running Windows Phone.
ab: For anyone wanting a cheap backup phone
Very low cost
Windows Phone is discontinued and unsupported

q.t: it's staggeringly cheap for a perfectly good phone.

t: Bright-Sided: How Positive Thinking Is Undermining America
s: A critique of the American cult of positive thinking, from self-help to corporate culture to the 2008 crash.
w: Recommended as a counterweight to relentless-positivity advice, especially in threads about depression and so-called abundant thinking.
ab: For skeptics of self-help and motivational culture
Journalistic and argumentative, not a how-to
Also touches on health and business culture

q.t: Barbara Ehrenreich wrote a good book about this subject:

t: Crucial Conversations: Tools for Talking When Stakes Are High
s: A guide to handling high-stakes, emotionally charged conversations at work and at home.
w: Regularly listed among books for new managers and for anyone facing difficult talks with co-workers or partners.
ab: For ICs becoming managers and anyone avoiding hard talks
Practical frameworks and scripts
Self-help style, somewhat formulaic

s: An American mother compares French and American parenting while raising her children in Paris.
w: Suggested to first-time parents who want a different style of parenting, often listed alongside other parenting books.
ab: For new parents curious about French methods
Anecdotal rather than scientific
Cultural generalizations

q.t: I enjoyed Bringing Up Bébé by Pamela Druckerman.

s: A critique of nutrition science and politics behind the food pyramid and low-fat diet advice.
w: Cited in low-fat versus low-carb debates; one commenter found it better than expected. Content is contested in nutrition circles.
ab: For readers curious about nutrition politics
Contrarian stance
Nutrition science has moved on; claims disputed

q.t: Denise Minger's book on the topic, Death by Food Pyramid

t: Things Might Go Terribly, Horribly Wrong
s: A guide to living with anxiety using acceptance and commitment therapy.
w: Offered to people stuck with worry or anxiety, though several recommenders have only heard good things about it.
ab: For anxious or stuck readers
Based on ACT
Not a replacement for therapy

s: An ethnography of ship navigation showing how cognition is distributed across people and tools.
w: Cited as research for distributed cognition and teamwork, and recommended for understanding how a ship's crew behaves as one intelligence.
ab: For UX and cognitive science readers
Naval navigation case study
Academic and dense

q.t: I would recommend Ed Hutchins' "Cognition in the Wild".

s: A friendly guide to real analysis aimed at students learning to read and write proofs.
w: Recommended as an amazing intro for those who are comfortable with proofs and want an approachable route into analysis.
ab: For self-learners starting real analysis
Study advice plus worked examples
Not a full textbook

q.t: How to Think About Analysis by Lara Alcock is an amazing intro to Analysis.

t: Object-Oriented Programming in Common Lisp: A Programmer's Guide to CLOS
s: A guide to CLOS, the Common Lisp Object System, covering classes, generic functions and the metaobject protocol.
w: Listed among the go-to resources for learning CLOS, alongside Practical Common Lisp.
ab: For Lisp programmers learning CLOS
Classic introduction from 1989
Dated style; check the Lisp references

w: Called fantastic for learning computer architecture from the ground up. Chips from the era are still available.
ab: For retrocomputing hobbyists
Hardware plus software, ground up
Vintage book; the parts are old

q.t: You will learn the basics of computer architecture, digital logic, assembly language, power supply design, and a basic operating system.

t: Introduction to 64 Bit Assembly Programming for Linux and OS X
s: A beginner-oriented introduction to x86-64 assembly on Linux and OS X.
w: Suggested as a beginner-friendly x64 assembly text. One reader says learning it was a revolution for them.
ab: For programmers learning assembly
Covers floating point and tuning
Some find the English awkward elsewhere in the list

q.t: Being able to read a little assembly was a revolution for me.

s: A plain-spoken guide to low-cost index investing, from the Bogleheads community that follows Vanguard founder John Bogle.
w: HN commenters tell newcomers to read it for basic investment literacy, with one calling it one of just two books you need to read and follow.
ab: For people starting to invest
Simple, repeatable index-fund approach
US-centric; fund details date quickly

q.t: you just need to read and obey two books and two books only

s: A reference with algorithms for converting between the world's calendars, including Gregorian, Julian, Islamic, Hebrew and Chinese.
w: HN's answer for anyone writing date code: it has far more detail on calendars than most people will want, which is the point.
ab: For developers handling dates and calendars
Algorithms for many world calendars
Heavy reference, not a casual read

q.t: There's a nice book that has way more detail on this than most people actually would want

s: A guide to building standardized, reliable and observable microservices, from the author's time at Uber.
w: Listed in HN reading lists on microservices architecture; during the Uber story, commenters urged people to buy the book.
ab: For engineers running microservices
Standards for reliability and monitoring
Short on deep architecture theory

t: Flights of Fantasy: Programming 3D Video Games in C++

ab: For retro dev and nostalgia
Teaches 3D from scratch
Very dated tooling (DOS, Borland C++)

ab: For geometry lovers and design fans
Colorful diagrams in place of letters
Keeps original errors, corrected at the start

s: A compact folding Bluetooth keyboard for phones and tablets.
w: HN travelers like it as a pocketable keyboard for phones. Both fans say it's not for extended typing.
ab: For travel and phone typing
Folds small enough for a pocket
Not for long typing sessions

t: Learning Resources Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set
s: A screen-free programmable toy mouse that kids steer through a maze by entering simple step sequences on its back.

Mouse, maze pieces and cheese; no screen needed
Maze setups take space; older kids outgrow it

Cheap and sticks to most surfaces

Soft silicone, cheap

NDIR sensor, 0-3000 ppm

ab: For nostalgic web designers
Visual
IE6-era techniques

Shallow compared with deep technical books

Written for older Scala versions

Edited collection
Reference, not a course

Manning book
Lift's popularity has faded

s: A Manning book on building real-time web apps with the Meteor framework.

Real-time apps
Meteor has declined

Pre-deep-learning NLP

Advocacy book; mainstream economists disagree

One side's account; read with that in mind

May be out of print

s: A documentary about Jiro Ono, an 85-year-old Tokyo sushi master, and his obsessive pursuit of perfecting his craft.

Documentary about a small Tokyo sushi restaurant

Shallow by design; use it to find models to study deeper

Higher level than introductory texts

s: A folding electric scooter.

Pricey
